title: Invocation Harmonizer: stable tool/function identifiers and streaming-safe aliases
text:
Invocation Harmonizer: stable tool/function identifiers and streaming-safe aliases

description:
Problem: OpenAI-style 'tools' and our legacy 'functions' can be invoked by a mix of names, aliases, and informal parameters. In cross-version usage we see collisions, ambiguous routing, and failed streaming handshakes when the name used at inference time doesn't match the stored function signature.

This ticket defines the Invocation Harmonizer service: a thin registry + runtime adapter that issues and resolves stable identifiers for callable surfaces (tools/functions), supports aliasing and historical names, and provides streaming-safe invocation envelopes. The service will: (1) generate canonical stable IDs (human-readable + hash suffix) for every discovered callable, (2) maintain alias mappings (OpenAI tool names, legacy function names, historical variants), (3) perform signature normalization and safe coercion rules at the boundaries, (4) expose a runtime lookup used by the router and streaming proxy so chunked outputs can be correlated to the target callable without relying on fragile textual names.

Why different: unlike previous proposals that focused on name-normalizers, this one emphasizes a durable identifier and streaming-safe handshake that survives name collisions, cross-protocol calls, and gradual rollouts. It also embeds telemetry fields to backfill which alias was used and when a signature coercion happened.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Registry CRUD: can create canonical id for a callable and add/remove aliases; 2) Runtime adapter: router and streaming proxy can resolve alias->canonical id within 5ms median; 3) Backwards compatibility: legacy function calls that use old names route to the same runner with no change to user-visible outputs; 4) Streaming: streaming invocations include the canonical id in the initial handshake and subsequent chunks include a short token to tie them to the registry entry; 5) Tests: end-to-end test that simulates name collisions and fallback semantics; 6) Rollout: canary in one region with telemetry flag and automated rollback on error rate spike.

progress_updates:
2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting with runtime, router, and console teams. Agreed to use human-readable prefix + sha256( namespace+name+signature ) as canonical id format.
2026-02-22: PoC registry implemented (in-memory) and integrated into local router; basic alias resolution works for static calls.
2026-02-24: Streaming handshake spec documented and reviewed by infra; added short stream_token (8 bytes) appended to chunk headers to avoid including full canonical id on every chunk.
2026-02-26: Signature coercion rules drafted (type coercion, missing optional params, extra param stripping). Security asked for explicit allowlist for coercions — added to open questions.
2026-02-28: Integrated registry lookup into streaming proxy in staging; observed median resolution 3.6ms. Preparing PR for code review.

review_comments:
Sofia Ramirez (PRD review): Ensure product team can control alias visibility to customers — need admin UI to hide internal aliases.
Evan Brooks (Security): Add audit log entries for every registry mutation and for any coercion that changes parameters; require KMS-backed signing for canonical id issuance in private deployments.
Maya Kline (Runtime): Concern about registry becoming single point of failure — we should cache resolved ids in the router with TTL and fallback to last-known mapping on transient failures.
Dylan Wu (Observability): Add tracing fields: invocation.registry_id, invocation.alias, invocation.coercion_applied. Put a sample dashboard and alert playbook in the runbook.

test_plan:
Unit tests for registry CRUD and alias resolution; integration test that runs a model in streaming mode invoking a tool via (a) canonical id, (b) historical alias, and (c) conflicting alias to verify deterministic conflict resolution. Load test: 10k lookups/sec with cache disabled to validate latency tail. Chaos test: registry unavailability should cause router to use cached mapping and surface a controlled 503 after TTL expiry.

rollout_plan:
1) Deploy registry service in staging and enable opt-in via feature flag invocation_harmonizer_v1; 2) Canary in us-east-1 for 2 days at 2% traffic, monitor invocation.errors, coercion.rate, resolution.latency; 3) Expand to 25% across regions and enable cache warming; 4) Full rollout with 7-day observability window. If errors > 0.5% or resolution.latency P99 > 100ms, immediately roll back to previous routing behavior and open incident.

notes:
Decision: canonical id format = 'invocation:<scope>:<shortname>-<8char_hex_suffix>' where suffix = first 8 chars of sha256(namespace + name + normalized_signature).
To support private deployments we will export a signed registry snapshot (gzipped JSON) and a signed timestamp. Private control planes will validate registry signatures with tenant KMS keys.
We will not rename existing public tool names; instead we map them to canonical ids and surface migration suggestions to SDKs to start returning canonical ids for new tooling calls.
Follow-up: design small admin UI for alias management and audit history (PM/Design ticket to be opened).
